fatal_errors: The proposed Cu interlayer is absent from the target system; the relevant material is an FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer made from Al0.2CrFeNi and Al targets.
The hypothesis replaces modulation-period-controlled coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary-dominated interfaces with an invented HEA/Cu architecture.
It invokes elevated-temperature diffusion, whereas the reported transition was observed during room-temperature nanoindentation creep.

The proposed mechanism has the wrong coherency relationship: the target attributes diffusion/interface-slip-mediated creep to the semicoherent 16 nm multilayer, while coherent and grain-boundary-dominated samples remain primarily dislocation-mediated.
No evidence is cited for Cu diffusivity, coherent HEA/Cu interfaces, or the claimed crossover.
explanation: The response recognizes that interface coherency can govern a crossover between diffusion- and dislocation-mediated creep, but it does not reconstruct the studied material or result. The target is the 16 nm modulation-period Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer, whose semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces contain misfit dislocations. Their strong obstruction of glide and associated stress concentration were proposed to promote interfacial amorphization and atomic diffusion or interface slip, producing low stress exponents and the strongest creep resistance. The generated hypothesis instead introduces Cu, elevated temperatures, and a crossover toward dislocation creep at coherent interfaces. Those claims are neither supported by the supplied evidence nor consistent with the target conditions and mechanism. Its proposed thickness/temperature/stress matrix with microscopy and direct dislocation observations is reasonably falsifiable as a new research idea, but it remains an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
